title: Translate one scenario pack into one language (qualified-speaker + back-translation for Tier C)
context: This is the first end-to-end pack: one scenario pack translated into one target language with full provenance, attribution, the mandatory disclaimer verbatim, and tier-appropriate review. It proves the whole pipeline except final field adoption. It is hard-gated on license-000 passing before any drafting begins.
objective: Translate one scenario pack into one target language as a complete, reviewed, correctly-licensed pack.
acceptanceCriteria: license-000 passed before drafting; locale-001 emergency number verified and injected
One scenario pack translated in full into one target language, UTF-8; preserved tokens (numbers, units, body parts, emergency number) preserved exactly; register/gender per glossary

Ships provenance.yaml (phrase ids, sources/original records, versions, glossary + locale versions, translator, reviewers) and attribution.txt (attribution + mandatory disclaimer verbatim in target and pivot language)
Agent UNCERTAIN: flags captured into review.yaml as agentFlags; no sign-off while any flag is unresolved

Qualified-speaker sign-off recorded in the PR, reviewer independent of drafting (COI declared); Tier B/C get an independent second reviewer; every Tier-C phrase has a back-translation record; medical-critical Tier-C phrases have clinician/medical-interpreter sign-off
License/attribution check passes; output license correct (CC-BY-SA-4.0 / source-compatible)
output: packs/<scenario>/<lang>/<locale>/ (phrases.yaml, pack.pdf, pack.md, provenance.yaml, attribution.txt, review.yaml)
outputLicense: Source-compatible: CC-BY-SA-4.0 for project-original phrases; source-mandated license + mandatory disclaimer where derived (e.g. WHO CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO) — never relicensed as a more permissive license
